selects.description: Which ARIA pattern the row is: none is a toolbar of unrelated tools, single is a radiogroup of mutually exclusive choices, multiple is a plain group of independent toggles. It chooses the pattern and the keyboard; it does NOT own the selection. Every shipped call site keeps the selected value in the host, so in single the group clicks the child an arrow lands on and lets the host decide what that means. In single the host must also give every child a checked prop of "true" or "false": a radiogroup's required owned element is a radio, and jx-action-button becomes one only when checked is non-empty — a group of bare buttons is announced as a radiogroup with no checked member at all.

compact.description: Draw the children joined into one segmented control, sharing their inner borders and rounding only the outer corners. The group draws every member's frame and fill itself, whatever the member's own quiet says: a strong border round an input fill, the selected member in the accent tint with an accent edge (the solid accent with emphasized), and 4px of inline padding on a small member that shows text and no glyph, because the small size's 2px ran "Edit" into "Design". A member's quiet has no effect here. Off leaves them as separate buttons with a gap, each drawing itself, so a row of borderless tools is compact=false, never a compact group of quiet members. This is the one thing no button can do about itself: joining N of them needs selectors about a child's position among its siblings. The seam is a DIRECT-CHILD rule: it reaches the buttons the group itself owns — a slot leaves no node, so a distributed child is one — and so a nested group keeps its own compact, and a button a surface wraps in a div of its own is roved but not joined.

label.description: The accessible name of the group, and it is not optional in practice: a toolbar, a radiogroup and a group are all containers a reader is told they have entered, and an unnamed one is announced by its role alone. Nothing lints its absence — a bound role switches the naming rules off — so the element's own test pins it instead.

orientation.description: horizontal or vertical. It chooses which arrow pair moves the caret, and it turns both the layout and the segmented seam through 90 degrees off data-orientation. It also sets aria-orientation, but only where ARIA permits one: role=group — what selects="multiple" resolves to — supports neither aria-orientation nor its inheritance, and Chrome drops the attribute there, so writing it anyway would be an aria-allowed-attr violation in a consumer's own axe run.

onKeydown.description: The group keyboard contract: the arrow along its own axis moves the roving caret between enabled children with wrap, Home and End go to the ends, and in selects=single the child that takes the caret is clicked.

onReady.description: Collapses the group to one tab stop once it has rendered, and keeps it collapsed to one as children come and go. It listens for the element's own jx-ready because onMount is handed the reactive scope alone, and placing a caret needs the host.

emits.name: jx-ready
emits.description: The group has rendered and distributed its children, so its caret can be placed.

onMount.description: Announces that the element has rendered. The group's own onReady listens for it, and a host may too.

&[data-compact] > jx-action-button:not([.$description: The frame is the group's, not the member's. Every seam rule above acts on a member's border, and jx-action-button is quiet by default (a transparent border and fill, which is what a toolbar wants), so the shared borders, the rounded ends and the -1px overlap all worked on borders nobody could see, and a compact group drew as a gap-less row of bare words: the Canvas view switch, the Style panel's Display row, Preferences' Theme, the zoom pod and every other group Studio converted from Spectrum, whose sp-action-button was NOT quiet by default, so the conversion dropped the frame without anybody writing it off. So the group draws its members whatever their quiet says, which is what ui.md §5.4 means by `compact` with `single` being the segmented control. This rule and the selected one below are mutually exclusive, so neither depends on sheet order against the member's own; at (0,4,1) under the scope handle each outranks the member's quiet and selected rules at (0,3,0) and quiet's hover at (0,4,0). The ink restates the member's resting colour at this specificity so that only the hover rule below, which leaves a disabled member alone, can raise it: the member's own hover is not gated on disabled, and a disabled segment brightening under the pointer reads as one that can act.

The hover wash is LAYERED over the input fill rather than replacing it, as the member's own hover does. `--jx-hover-bg` is 6% of the ink over transparent, so on its own it shows whatever stands behind the group, and on the zoom pod's darkest background that came out a shade from the resting fill: a hover that did not read. As an image over the fill it is always the resting colour plus the wash, in both schemes.

&[data-compact] > jx-action-button[data-.$description: The chosen segment: the accent tint with an accent EDGE. The member's own selected state is a 15% tint and nothing else, which beside a bordered neighbour read as a faint wash rather than as the one that is on. Raised over both neighbours, so the accent edge shows on every side through the -1px overlap, and still under a focus ring. A hovered selected segment stays as it is: this outranks the member's quiet hover.
The member's emphasized, kept: the solid accent, edge and all.

A small member that shows no glyph is a text segment, and the small size's inline padding is 2px, which is right for a 20px glyph button and ran the words of a text row together ("flex" into "grid"). A text segment takes --jx-space-2 instead. Keyed on the hidden icon part, so an icon segment keeps its square shape, and scoped to the group rather than made the small size's own, because some forty other small text buttons in Studio would widen with it; the widest Style panel row measured 220px of its 256px with this padding, and would overflow at --jx-space-3. An engine without :has() keeps the 2px.

&[data-compact] > jx-action-button > [pa.$description: Over everything, the selected segment's raised edge included, so a focus ring is never painted under a neighbour.

&[data-compact] > jx-action-button[data-.$description: A small action button carries a `::before` that extends its hit area 2px past its drawn box on every side (an inset of -3px: the button's 1px border, then half the 4px it is under, because an absolutely positioned box is offset from the padding edge), so that a 20px picture accepts the pointer over the kit's 24px control height (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8, ui.md §4.3). In a compact group the boxes TOUCH on the packed axis — no gap, and each border drawn over the last — so an extension there could reach nothing but the neighbour's own box, and the later sibling paints above the earlier one: the last 2px of every button but the last would activate the button after it. The criterion gives an overlapped area to the target on TOP, so the extension would buy the earlier button nothing and cost it a stolen strip. The default 2px gap is the other case: two extensions overlap by 2px there, the later member keeps the strip, and every small member but the last counts 22px on the packed axis, which is under the floor and which ui.md §11 names beside this one. The packed axis is therefore zeroed here — `0` is the padding edge, 1px inside the drawn border, and the button's own box accepts the pointer over that pixel — and the cross axis keeps its 2px past the drawn box, which reaches only the gap around the group: a compact group's small members are 24px tall and as wide as they draw, which ui.md §11 records as the one thing the technique cannot reach. The vertical variant swaps the axes, and its inline value is the button's own -3px for the same reason.

The chosen segment, redrawn. Forced colours replace every author colour with the user's palette, so the accent tint and the accent edge both collapse into the ones around them and the segmented control would say nothing about which segment is on. The system's own selection pair says it instead, as jx-switch does for its checked track.
